headline: China's CXMT memory design claim turned into a regional rout on Tuesday, with the Kospi down 5.57 percent and Samsung Electronics down 10.5 percent in morning trade after Monday's 0.44 percent Nasdaq decline, while the rupee posted its sharpest session since June at 95.76 per dollar after the RBI routed about 10 billion dollars of monthly state refiner demand away from the spot market.

summary.us: The S&P 500 closed Monday at 7,807.24, down 0.06 percent, the Nasdaq Composite at 27,245.90, down 0.44 percent, and the Dow at 51,850.55, up 0.38 percent, as memory and semiconductor names sold off after China's CXMT described a denser DRAM design at a Shanghai conference on Oct 10, with Micron down 3.88 percent, CrowdStrike down 4.37 percent and Arm down 4.15 percent. Energy led nine of eleven sectors higher as WTI settled about 2 percent up at 93.74 dollars on an attack on Riyadh's airport, the Treasury market was shut for Columbus Day with the 10 year yield at 5.24 percent, and JPMorgan, Goldman Sachs, Citigroup and Wells Fargo report before Tuesday's open.
summary.india: The Nifty closed Monday at 22,363.35, down 0.70 percent, and Bank Nifty at 54,918, down 0.61 percent, after the RBI raised the minimum daily cash reserve ratio maintenance to 99 percent from 90 percent effective Oct 16 and scheduled a 25,000 crore rupee bond sale for Oct 13, which hit lenders with SBI down 2.06 percent to 939.30 rupees and ICICI Bank down 1.37 percent to 1,336.50 rupees. September CPI printed at 5.54 percent against 4.83 percent in August with food inflation at 7.74 percent, foreign investors sold a net 1,708 crore rupees against 3,045 crore rupees of domestic buying on a twelfth straight selling day, and the rupee rallied to 95.76 per dollar.
summary.global: Seoul and Tokyo carried the chip selloff into Tuesday, with the Kospi down 5.57 percent at 6,028.66 after a 3.65 percent fall on Monday to 6,384.24 and the Nikkei 225 down 2.59 percent at 67,242.69, while Samsung Electronics fell 10.5 percent to 234,500 won on a fifth session of foreign selling tied to Chinese memory progress and AI capex cost doubts. Monday's closes elsewhere were firmer, with the Hang Seng up 0.25 percent at 24,271.20, the Stoxx 600 up 0.65 percent at 635.65 as a 1.5 percent gain in bank shares offset the oil move, the FTSE 100 up 0.99 percent and the DAX up 0.76 percent, and the dollar index rose 0.25 percent to 102.47.

weekly.narrative: The week turned on the long end of the Treasury curve, where yields pushed to multi year highs midweek and the 30 year auction cleared at 5.618 percent, the highest since August 2000, before solid demand cooled the move and let the S&P 500 finish 1.15 percent higher and the Nasdaq 0.64 percent higher despite a Thursday air pocket when the Financial Times reported OpenAI annualized revenue about 20 billion dollars below the figure circulated to investors. India spent the week absorbing the RBI's first rate hike since February 2023, a 25 basis point move to 5.50 percent on Oct 7 paired with a hawkish calibrated tightening stance and an FY27 CPI forecast lifted to 5.2 percent, which left the Nifty up only 0.44 percent while Bank Nifty gained 1.48 percent and foreign investors kept selling, including a 12,944 crore rupee outflow on Oct 8. Metals were the cleanest trade, with copper up 3.37 percent on the Centinela strike in Chile and Chinese restocking, and silver and gold adding 1.89 and 1.39 percent as real yields retreated into Friday. Crypto went the other way, bitcoin down 2.58 percent and ether down 7.34 percent on the week, pressured by high oil costs, rate hike expectations and Middle East risk. Next week brings the first real test of earnings season, with JPMorgan and Citigroup on Oct 13 and Bank of America on Oct 14, alongside US September CPI on Oct 14 that the street expects at 3.6 percent on the year, India September CPI, and TSMC results on Oct 15.
